message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a written move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord withholds any portion. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary, and livable condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, pest control). | • Report problems in writing (email or text) and give the landlord a reasonable time to fix them. | | **Repair & Maintenance** | • If the landlord fails to repair, you may:
 1. **Withhold rent** (only after giving written notice and a 10‑day cure period).
 2. **Repair and deduct** (pay for the repair and deduct the cost from rent).
 3. **Sue for damages** if the issue is serious. | • Keep receipts and document the problem. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • File a complaint if the landlord repeatedly enters without notice or causes disturbances. | | **Notice Requirements** | • **Rent increases**: Must be in writing and given at least **30 days** before the increase takes effect.
• **Eviction**: Must follow the Texas Property Code §92.001‑92.006. Typically, a 30‑day notice for non‑payment or a 60‑day notice for lease termination. | • Verify the notice is in writing and delivered properly (hand‑delivery, certified mail, or posting). | | **Lease Termination** | • You can terminate a month‑to‑month lease with **30 days’ written notice**.
• Landlords can terminate only for reasons listed in the Texas Property Code (e.g., non‑payment, violation of lease, landlord’s intent to occupy). | • Provide written notice and keep a copy. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income (Fair Housing Act). | • File a complaint with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or the Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Privacy** | • Landlords must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of all entries and request a written explanation if you suspect unlawful entry. | | **Security Deposit Deductions** | • Deductions must be for:
 1. Unpaid rent
 2. Damage beyond normal wear and tear
 3. Cleaning costs if the unit was left dirty
 4. Replacement of lost keys or locks | • If you disagree, file a claim in the Texas Small Claims Court (up to $20,000). | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has **no statewide rent control**; rent can be increased at any time, subject to the notice requirements above. | • Negotiate lease terms or seek local ordinances that may offer protections. | | **Legal Remedies** | • **Small Claims Court**: For disputes up to $20,000.
• **Civil Court**: For larger claims or eviction disputes.
• **Mediation**: Many counties offer free or low‑cost mediation services. | • Gather documentation (photos, receipts, correspondence) before filing. | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Moving In 1. **Get a written lease** – Even if it’s a month‑to‑month agreement, a written document protects both parties. 2. **Document the condition** – Take photos or video of the unit and keep a copy of the move‑in inspection report. 3. **Ask about the security deposit** – Confirm the amount and the conditions for its return. 4. **Know your local ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional tenant protections. #### When You Encounter a Problem 1. **Notify the landlord in writing** (email or certified mail). 2. **Give a reasonable cure period** (usually 10 days for repairs). 3. **Keep records** – Save all correspondence, receipts, and photos. 4. **Seek legal help** if the landlord fails to comply. --- ### Resources | Resource | What It Offers | How to Access | |----------|----------------|---------------| | **Texas Property Code** | Statutory rights and obligations | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights** | Discrimination complaints | https://www.tchra.org/ | | **HUD Fair Housing Hotline** | Federal discrimination complaints | https://www.hud.gov/ | | **Texas Small Claims Court** | Filing small claims | https://www.txcourts.gov/small-claims/ | | **Local Tenant Associations** | Advocacy and support | Search online for your city’s tenant association | --- #### Bottom Line As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, a fair security deposit process, proper notice for rent changes or eviction, and protection against discrimination. Keep everything in writing, document everything, and don’t hesitate to use the legal remedies available if your landlord violates your rights.
